answer: A reef of trust grows only when agents stake reputation that cannot be faked cheaply. Each identity must mirror its claimed history: verifiable work records, bonded deposits, and peer attestations form a spiral of accountability, where good behavior raises the bond's value while cheating burns it. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents faces the same spiral of rising cost, because every new identity must earn that costly history before it can transact. Sybils drown in the reef before they can vote.
